module_title: Market Indices (Sensex & Nifty) and Market Capitalization
introduction: It is impossible to track the daily price changes of all 5000+ listed companies. Therefore, we use an 'Index' (a statistical barometer) to measure the overall health and direction of the stock market.

core_concepts.title: SENSEX (Sensitive Index)
core_concepts.description: It is the benchmark index of the BSE. It consists of the '30 largest' and most actively traded, financially sound companies listed on the BSE. If the Sensex is up, it generally means India's top 30 companies are growing.

core_concepts.title: NIFTY 50
core_concepts.description: It is the flagship index of the NSE. The word is a blend of 'National + Fifty'. It tracks the performance of '50 major companies' spanning 12 different sectors of the Indian economy.

core_concepts.title: Market Capitalization (Market Cap)
core_concepts.description:
This determines the total monetary value of a company. 
Formula: (Total Outstanding Shares) x (Current Price of One Share). 
Based on this, companies are categorized into Large-Cap (most stable), Mid-Cap, and Small-Cap (highly volatile).

core_concepts.title: Blue-Chip Companies
core_concepts.description: These are massive, nationally recognized, well-established, and financially sound companies (e.g., Reliance, TCS, HDFC). They form the core of the Sensex and Nifty indices and are considered safe investments.

important_entities.name: Listing
important_entities.description: A company cannot simply start trading on an exchange. It must go through an IPO and fulfill strict SEBI guidelines to get 'listed' on the BSE or NSE.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Examiners frequently swap the numbers in 'Match the Following' questions. Remember: SENSEX = 30 companies. NIFTY = 50 companies.

mnemonics_and_tricks.memory_phrase: Sensex started deep in the past (1978)
mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: The base year for calculating Sensex is 1978-79 (Base value = 100). The base year for Nifty is 1995 (Base value = 1000).

exam_strategy_tips: Both Sensex and Nifty are calculated using the 'Free-Float Market Capitalization' method (counting only the shares available for public trading, excluding promoter shares). This specific technical term is a favorite in banking exams.
